title: What changed when I split AI-generated slot art into layers for Android
author: gazman_dev
selftext:
I’m building Slots X26: Wild Worlds in libGDX. I started by using ImageGen to explore the whole screen, but the paintings were hard to use as the screen itself. The reels, coin count, and Spin button all need to move or update independently. For the production art I generated the paintings separately, then used a script to crop the transparent edges and pack the layers without stretching them.



One concrete example: the jungle companion can lean over the reels. In the mock that overlap was painted in. In the game the character is a separate layer, and the live Spin button draws above it. That let me keep the pose on short landscape phones without painting a fake button into each image. If you’ve used ImageGen for game UI, how do you handle overlaps between art and controls that need to stay tappable?



I’d also love a first-run check from a few Android players (18+). Try five minutes and tell me whether it was obvious how to pick a companion and start spinning. If you quit early, what was the last screen you saw? It’s a free simulated-slots game with virtual coins, optional purchases and no cash prizes. A comment here is plenty.



Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gazman.slots26](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gazman.slots26)
